Prealgebra · Lesson 12.2

Make an Organized List

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Some problems have no formula behind them. They ask what is possible, and the only way to answer is to write every possibility down. The hard part is not missing any. So instead of scribbling possibilities as they come to mind, pick an order first, work through it step by step, and stop only when the order runs out. Then you know the list is complete. This lesson is about writing lists that way.

Problem
At an arcade counter, plushies cost 1212 tickets and keychains cost 55 tickets. A player spends exactly 5353 tickets. How many plushies did the player buy?
Show a hint
  • Try each plushie count in turn, 0,1,2,3,40,1,2,3,4, and check whether the remaining tickets are a multiple of 55.
  • A multiple of 55 ends in 00 or 55, which makes each leftover instant to test.
Show the full solution

Try plushie counts from zero and check the leftover. Zero leaves 5353, one leaves 4141, two leave 2929, three leave 1717, and none of those are multiples of 55. Four plushies cost 4848, leaving 53−48=553−48=5, which is exactly one keychain, so 44​ plushies.

Five plushies would already cost 6060, more than the total, so the list ends there and the answer is unique.

Problem
At a juice bar, smoothies cost 99 tokens and juices cost 66 tokens. A camp counselor spends exactly 6060 tokens and buys at least one drink of some kind, possibly zero of one kind. How many different orders are possible?
Show a hint
  • March through the number of smoothies, 0,1,2,…0,1,2,…, and for each one check whether the leftover tokens split evenly into 66s.
Show the full solution

Walk the smoothie count upward and test each leftover. Zero leaves 6060, which is 1010 juices. One leaves 5151, not a multiple of 66. Two leave 4242, which is 77 juices. Three leave 3333, no. Four leave 2424, which is 44 juices. Five leave 1515, no. Six leave 66, one juice. Seven would cost more than 6060. That is 44​ orders.

Marching the smoothie count from 00 to 66 without skipping is what guarantees nothing was missed.

Key idea
Vary one quantity at a time. When two unknowns share one total, do not change both at once. Pick one, usually the pricier item, and count it up from zero one step at a time. Each step fixes the leftover, and that leftover either divides evenly among the other item or it does not. Going in order means the finished table holds every combination that works and no others.
smoothiesjuices
010
27
44
61
Problem
How many two-digit numbers have digits that multiply to 1212?
Show a hint
  • List the factor pairs of 1212 where both factors are single digits, then remember each pair can appear in two orders.
Show the full solution

Digit pairs multiplying to 1212 must be factor pairs with both factors at most 99, so 2×62×6 and 3×43×4. The pair 1×121×12 fails, since 1212 is not a digit.

Each surviving pair builds two numbers, 2626 and 6262, 3434 and 4343.

44​

Problem
A puzzle card reads, find the two-digit number that is a multiple of 99, has both digits prime, and has a ones digit larger than its tens digit. What is the number?
Show a hint
  • Start from the tightest condition. There are only ten two-digit multiples of 99, so list them.
  • The prime digits are 2,3,5,72,3,5,7. Strike out every multiple of 99 containing any other digit, then apply the last condition.
Show the full solution

The two-digit multiples of 99 are 18,27,36,45,54,63,72,81,90,9918,27,36,45,54,63,72,81,90,99. Both digits must be prime, so both come from 2,3,5,72,3,5,7, and only 2727 and 7272 survive. The ones digit has to be larger than the tens digit, which leaves 2727​.

Starting from the multiples of 99 meant checking ten numbers instead of all ninety.

Key idea
Start with the tightest condition. When a problem stacks several conditions, check which one leaves the fewest candidates. Multiple of 99 leaves only ten two-digit numbers, while ones digit larger than tens digit leaves dozens. Build your master list from the tight condition, then use the looser ones to cross entries off. Running it the other way still works, but you would be testing ninety numbers instead of ten.
Problem
A snack stand offers 66 different toppings, and a frozen yogurt comes with exactly 22 different toppings. Using an alphabetical list or otherwise, count how many different topping pairs are possible.
Show a hint
  • Name the toppings A through F and list pairs alphabetically, all pairs starting with A first, then those starting with B, and so on.
  • A starts 55 pairs, B starts 44 new ones, and each later letter starts one fewer.
Show the full solution

Go in alphabetical order. Pairs starting with A are AB, AC, AD, AE, AF, five of them. Pairs starting with B add BC, BD, BE, BF, four new ones, since AB is already counted. Each letter after that adds one fewer.

5+4+3+2+1=155+4+3+2+1=15​

This is the pairs count from the counting chapter, rebuilt by hand. If the formula slips your mind mid-problem, an organized list rebuilds it for you.

Problem
A street performer splits 77 identical juggling rings among 33 identical trays, with every tray holding at least one ring. Since the trays are identical, only the group sizes matter, not which tray is which. How many different splits are possible?
Show a hint
  • Sort each split from largest pile to smallest, and list splits in order of the largest pile, starting from the biggest it could be, which is 55.
  • For each choice of largest pile, march the middle pile downward and let the smallest pile be whatever remains, checking it stays between 11 and the middle.
Show the full solution

Write every split largest pile first. The largest pile can be at most 55, since the other two trays need a ring each.

Largest 55 forces 5,1,15,1,1. Largest 44 gives 4,2,14,2,1. Largest 33 gives 3,3,13,3,1 and 3,2,23,2,2. A largest pile of 22 could hold at most 2+2+2=62+2+2=6 rings, too few.

44​

Sorting each split before writing it is what stops 4,2,14,2,1 and 1,2,41,2,4 from sneaking in as two different entries.

Key idea
Sort the list by a fixed rule. Pick an ordering and hold to it. Largest pile first, smallest number first, and alphabetical order all work, as long as you stay consistent. The ordering stops the same possibility from being written twice in a different order, and it tells you when you are done, because the next entry would break the rule you chose.
largest traymiddlesmallest
511
421
331
322
Problem
A gym locker's number is between 3030 and 6060. Divided by 77 it leaves remainder 22, and divided by 44 it leaves remainder 11. What is the locker number?
Show a hint
  • The remainder-22 condition is the rarer one. List those numbers between 3030 and 6060 first, they climb by 77s.
  • That short list is 30,37,44,51,5830,37,44,51,58. Test each against the divided-by-44 condition.
Show the full solution

Numbers that leave remainder 22 when divided by 77 come every seven steps, so between 3030 and 6060 they are 30,37,44,51,5830,37,44,51,58. Their remainders under 44 run 2,1,0,3,22,1,0,3,2, and only 3737 leaves the required 11.

3737​

With two remainder conditions, list out the one that gives fewer candidates and let the other one filter.

Problem
How many three-digit numbers have digits adding to exactly 44?
Show a hint
  • Organize by the hundreds digit, which can be 1,2,3,1,2,3, or 44. Each choice leaves a smaller target for the last two digits.
  • With hundreds digit 11, the last two digits must add to 33, giving 03,12,21,3003,12,21,30, four numbers. Count the other cases the same way.
Show the full solution

Case on the hundreds digit. If it is 11, the remaining digits sum to 33, giving 103,112,121,130103,112,121,130, four numbers. If it is 22, they sum to 22, giving 202,211,220202,211,220, three numbers. If it is 33, two numbers, 301,310301,310. If it is 44, just 400400.

4+3+2+1=104+3+2+1=10​

The case counts step down 4,3,2,14,3,2,1, which is the kind of pattern an organized list often hands you for free.

Fun fact
There is a famous online encyclopedia whose entries are not words but lists of numbers. Type in the start of any sequence you have discovered, like 1,4,9,161,4,9,16, and it names the pattern, cites who found it, and shows where else it appears. Mathematicians add new lists to it nearly every day.
Problem
A librarian packs 88 identical books into identical boxes, using at most 33 boxes, with no box left empty. How many different packings are possible?
Show a hint
  • Split into cases by the number of boxes used, one, two, or three, and handle each case as its own ordered list.
  • With two boxes list 7+1,6+2,5+3,4+47+1,6+2,5+3,4+4 and stop before repeats. With three, march the largest pile from 66 down.
Show the full solution

One box gives a single packing, all 88 together.

Two boxes, written larger pile first, give 7+17+1, 6+26+2, 5+35+3, 4+44+4, and stopping there matters, since 3+53+5 would repeat 5+35+3. That is 44 packings.

Three boxes, marching the largest pile downward, give 6+1+16+1+1, 5+2+15+2+1, 4+3+14+3+1, 4+2+24+2+2, 3+3+23+3+2. That is 55 more.

1+4+5=101+4+5=10​

Problem
A padlock's three-digit code has strictly decreasing digits, is a multiple of 55, and has digits adding to 1212. How many codes fit all three conditions?
Show a hint
  • A multiple of 55 ends in 00 or 55, so split into those two cases.
  • Ending in 00 needs the first two digits to add to 1212 with first digit larger. Ending in 55 needs them to add to 77 with both digits larger than 55, which is worth checking carefully.
Show the full solution

Case one, the code ends in 00. The first two digits add to 1212, strictly decreasing into the 00, giving 93,84,7593,84,75, so the codes 930,840,750930,840,750.

Case two, the code ends in 55. The first two digits would add to 77 while each stays above 55, but two digits above 55 already add to at least 1313. The case is empty.

3+0=33+0=3​

An empty case is not wasted work. Proving nothing lives there is exactly what makes the final count trustworthy.

Key idea
Casework splits one big list into several short ones. Break the search along one natural feature, like the hundreds digit, the number of boxes, or how many of one item you buy. Each case becomes a short list you can finish quickly, and the case totals add at the end. Pick the splitting feature so that every possibility falls into exactly one case.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A bake sale prices muffins at 88 tokens and cookies at 55 tokens. One customer spends exactly 6767 tokens. How many muffins did the customer buy?
Show the solution

Marching muffins from zero, the leftovers run 67,59,51,43,35,27,19,11,367,59,51,43,35,27,19,11,3. Only 3535 ends in 00 or 55, at four muffins, leaving 77 cookies.

44​

Practice
How many two-digit multiples of 77 have digits adding to 1010?
Show the solution

The multiples run 14,21,28,35,42,49,56,63,70,77,84,91,9814,21,28,35,42,49,56,63,70,77,84,91,98. Checking digit sums, only 2828 and 9191 reach 1010.

22​

Practice
Six identical candles are packed into up to 33 identical gift bags, where a bag may hold any number of candles but empty bags are thrown away. Only the group sizes matter. How many different packings are possible?
Show the solution

One bag, just 66. Two bags, largest first, 5+15+1, 4+24+2, 3+33+3. Three bags, 4+1+14+1+1, 3+2+13+2+1, 2+2+22+2+2.

1+3+3=71+3+3=7​

Practice
A jersey number is less than 5050, leaves remainder 33 when divided by 88, and is a multiple of 55. What is the number?
Show the solution

Remainder 33 under 88 gives the list 3,11,19,27,35,433,11,19,27,35,43. The only multiple of 55 on it is 3535​.

Practice
How many two-digit numbers have digits adding to exactly 99?
Show the solution

For each tens digit 11 through 99, the ones digit must be 99 minus it, giving 18,27,36,45,54,63,72,81,9018,27,36,45,54,63,72,81,90, one number per tens digit.

99​

Practice
How many three-digit numbers use only the digits 1,2,3,41,2,3,4 with the digits strictly increasing from left to right?
Show the solution

Choosing which digit to leave out gives every possibility, 123,124,134,234123,124,134,234.

44​

Practice
An ice-cream cart offers 77 flavors, and a double cone holds 22 different flavors, order not mattering. How many different double cones are possible?
Show the solution

With the flavors ordered, the first starts 66 pairs, the second 55 new ones, then 4,3,2,14,3,2,1.

6+5+4+3+2+1=216+5+4+3+2+1=21​

Practice
How many three-digit palindromes smaller than 300300 are multiples of 44?
Show the solution

Palindromes 1x11x1 end in 11, which is odd, so no multiples of 44 live there. The 2x22x2 family is 202,212,222,232,242,252,262,272,282,292202,212,222,232,242,252,262,272,282,292.

A number is a multiple of 44 exactly when its last two digits are, so test 02,12,22,…02,12,22,… The survivors are 212,232,252,272,292212,232,252,272,292.

55​

Practice
At a fair, rides cost 1212 tickets and games cost 77 tickets. A visitor spends exactly 100100 tickets. How many rides and games did the visitor enjoy in total?
Show the solution

Marching rides, the leftovers are 100,88,76,64,52,40,28,16,4100,88,76,64,52,40,28,16,4, and only 2828, at six rides, is a multiple of 77, giving four games.

6+4=106+4=10​

Practice
A game shop sells power crystals in sizes 11, 55, and 1010 gems. In how many different ways can a player spend exactly 2525 gems, where only the number of each size matters?
Show the solution

Case on tens. With two tens, 55 gems remain, allowing zero or one five, 22 ways. With one ten, 1515 remain, allowing zero through three fives, 44 ways. With no tens, 2525 remain, allowing zero through five fives, 66 ways.

2+4+6=122+4+6=12​

The singles handle the cleanup, filling any remainder in exactly one way, so the whole count comes down to the tens and fives.
